key_insight: An operation-aware multimodal model combining patient data, clinical notes, and hospital workload signals achieved the strongest ICU readmission prediction performance among the evaluated approaches.
clinical_relevance: Accounting for hospital workload alongside patient condition may help contextualize ICU discharge risk, but clinical benefit remains unproven.
method: Combined workload and admission-flow indicators with vital signs, ICD/DRG codes, and clinical notes.
Used multi-agent extraction and self-evolving retrieval-augmented generation to remove note template noise.
Fine-tuned a multimodal Transformer with layer-wise freezing and differential learning rates; addressed imbalance through class reweighting and threshold calibration.
evidence_signal: Across 20 independent runs on 20,000 MIMIC-III ICU stays with approximately 10.5% readmissions, the best model achieved AUROC 0.8288 ± 0.0110, PR-AUC 0.4373 ± 0.0310, and F1 0.4757 ± 0.0196.
watch_item: Retrospective MIMIC-III results require external and prospective validation before use in discharge decisions.
paper_title: Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System for ICU Discharge Risk Assessment
